title: Willie's teacher, reading music, mouthpieces and horn
summary: She does not know who taught him but he read music well; she describes his arrangement cards, warmed mouthpieces and costly horn.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: With some of his music. Now I couldn't tell you so many different ones come. Some of them dead would come there and guide him. If I know it all or something was coming along, I'd have kept it all. But you know how it is when people beg you for something? Yeah, you can't keep everything. No, I couldn't keep them. And then I had to move from where I was on Bonita Street because the house comes to leaking, you see. And that made me have to move. Well, I had to move when I had to move, you see. I was wondering who his teacher was. Did he ever tell you what he was? Uh-uh. He never did tell me. He must have had one. He had a teacher. The Lord, he had them. He had some knowledge, alright. And he could read the notes and everything. He was like, oh, you know what he was doing? I was wondering who his teacher was. Did he ever tell you what he was?

Uh-uh. He never did tell me. He must have had one. He had a teacher. The Lord, he had them. He had some knowledge, alright. And he could read the notes and everything. He was like, oh, you know what he was doing? He had some knowledge, alright.
And he could read the notes and everything just as good as he could. He sure could read the notes. He must have had somebody to learn him, you know. He couldn't learn by himself. He had to learn.
He said he could make arrangements. He had the cards in there, right?

Yeah, he had cards. He fixed them cards his shop, you know. Fixed all that. Oh, God, you ought to see him with that thing up on his shoulder. The child was just particularly like that. If he was fixing, he'd go sit down and eat a meal. And I had to wash that bag, you know, and keep it clean. And he stick all that down there. He had a little thing on the side where he stick the oil for the put on his horn. Then he had two mouthpieces and he made, I had bags I made. Now in the wintertime I had to heat them on the fire. Now after he take them off the fire, he stick them where it stay warm. But you see, he changed the mouthpiece. You see, I couldn't sell the mouthpiece. I had to throw them away. And he paid extra for them mouthpieces. I'd like to have it myself.
You should have saved those. Those are still good.

Well, the mouthpieces, all that was good. He paid four and a half for them. Some guy more than you. And the horn would cost plenty money too. Oh, yeah. Don't you think he didn't pay plenty for his horn? I don't know. I had it the other day. I was looking at it and I said, I had it. And what I done with it, I don't know. Is it in that box? Yeah, that's the box it was in.
Well, we can look through it again. One by one. I'm looking through it.
I don't know where. I don't know where.
I think I'd know it if I'd see it too.
Oh, I know it. He got two little bars with it.
